DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://mwv.dilg.gov.ph OIL G OPINION LLs- S. mcl DIRECTOR MARIA LOISELLA E. LUCINO, CESO IV Regional Director, DILG-Regional Office XIII Purok I-A, Brgy. Doongan, Butuan City Dear RD Lucino: This has reference to your Memorandum dated February I, 2024, requesting guidance on the effects of failure to file SOCE, for the Municipality of Basilica, Dinagat Islands. Section 14 of Republic Act No. 71661, provides that: "SEC. 14. Statement of Contributions and Expenditures: Effect of Failure to File Statement. — Every candidate and treasurer of the political party shall, within thirty (30) days after the day of the election, file in duplicate with the offices of the Commission the full, true and itemized statement of all contributions and expenditures in connection with the election. No person elected to anv public office shall enter upon the duties of his office until he has filed the statement of contributions and expenditures herein required. The same prohibition shall apply if the political party which nominated the winning candidate falls to file the statement required herein within the period prescribed by this Act. Except candidates for elective barangay office, failure to file the statements or reports in connection with electoral contributions and expenditures as required herein shall constitute an administrative offense for which the offenders shall be liable to pay an administrative fine ranging from One thousand pesos (PI,OOO.OO) to Thirty thousand pesos (P30,OOO.00), in the discretion of the Commission. The fine shall be paid within thirty (30) days from receipt of notice of such failure; otherwise, it shall be enforceable by a writ of execution issued by the Commission against the properties of the offender. It shall be the duty of every city or municipal election registrar to advise in writing, by personal delivery or registered mail, within five (5) days from the 1 Entitled: An Act Providing For Synchronized National And Local Elections And For Electoral Reforms, Authorizing Appropriations Therefor, And For Other Purposes. "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

date of election all candidates residing in his jurisdiction to comply with their obligation to file their statements of contributions and expenditures. For the commission of a second or subsequent offense under this section, the administrative fine shall be from Two thousand pesos (P2,OOO.00) to Sixty thousand pesos (P60,OOO.00), in the discretion of the Commission. In addition, the offender shall be subject to perpetual disqualification to hold public office. The mandatory nature of the foregoing Section 14 is clear from its letter. Second paragraph thereof prohibits winning candidates from assuming office should they fail to file their SOCE beyond the 30-day period after the day of the election. Correspondingly, COMELEC Resolution 105052, dated February 28, 2019, discusses the effect of failure to file SOCE. To quote: "SECTION. 13. Section 6 Rule 10 of the COMELEC Resolution No. 9991 as amended, is hereby amended to read as follows: SECTION 1. Effect of failure to file SOCE. — No elected candicate shall enter upon the duties of office until he filed his SOCE. The same prohibition shall apply if the electoral party which nominated the winning candidate fails to file SOCE. Except candidates for elective barangay and sk offices, failure to file SOCE shall constitute an administrative offense for which the offender shall be liable to pay an administrative fine in accordance with the Scale of Administrative Fine under Section II hereof. The fine shall be paid within thirty (30) days from receipt of notice of such failure; otherwise, it shall be enforceable by a writ of execution issued by the CFO against the properties of the offender. xxx The office of an elected candidate who failed to file SOCE shall be considered vacant pursuant to Section II of the Omnibus Election Code until he has complied and submitted his SOCE within six months from proclamation. After the lapse of said period and the candidate failed to assume office, a permanent vacancy occurs for which said office shall be filled up in accordance with the Constitution or law. " As can be gleaned from above, the office of an elected candidate who failed to file his/her SOCE shall be considered "vacant," for the winning candidate's failure to assume pursuant to Section 11 of the Omnibus Election Code (OEC), until he has complied and submitted his SOCE within six months from proclamation. Apropos, until the filing of the SOCE, the situation is more of temporary vacancy which shall be filled up in accordance 2 Entitled: Amendment to the Omnibus Rules and Regulations Governing Campaign Finance and Disclosure Page 2 of 3

with Section 19 (c) of Republic Act No. 10742, otherwise known as the Sangguniang Kabataan Reform Act of 2015, as amended by Republic Act No. 11768 It bears emphasis that after the lapse of six months and the candidate failed to assume office, a permanent vacancy occurs for which said office shall be filled up in accordance with the law. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: J ANVI R R. LLAMAS Un r cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs O LLAJJVRULLLS-LRALLDOvpr Page 3 of3
